title: Browsers Block eMudhra Intermediate CAs Over Recoverable Private Keys
description: Eight intermediate certificates issued by Indian CA eMudhra in April 2025 had their private keys compromised due to weak cryptographic entropy during key generation. Major browsers and root programs including Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome, Apple, and Microsoft have blocked these certificates. The compromised keys could allow attackers to forge trusted HTTPS certificates and impersonate websites. eMudhra revoked the certificates and communicated the issue to downstream trust stores. Some clients may require software updates to fully remove trust in these compromised intermediates. The flaw originated from a script error during the key generation ceremony, producing weak keys mistakenly used in certificate signing requests.
aiSummary: In April 2025, eMudhra issued eight intermediate certificates whose private keys were compromised due to insufficient randomness in key generation. The weak keys were effectively all-zeroes except for the last byte and could be recovered quickly using the baby-step giant-step discrete log algorithm. This vulnerability enables attackers to forge trusted HTTPS certificates to impersonate any website for clients still trusting these intermediates. Major browsers (Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome, Apple Safari, Microsoft Edge) blocked these certificates between October 17 and October 20, 2026. eMudhra revoked the certificates and is investigating code and process flaws in their key lifecycle management. Although no evidence of malicious use was found in Certificate Transparency logs, some clients may still trust the compromised certificates until updated.
aiImpact: Attackers with access to the compromised private keys could generate fraudulent TLS certificates trusted by affected clients, enabling impersonation of any website. This undermines the trust model of HTTPS and could facilitate man-in-the-middle attacks against users trusting these intermediates. While major browsers and trust stores have blocked and revoked the certificates, clients that have not updated their trust stores remain vulnerable. No confirmed malicious use has been observed in public logs, but the risk remains until all clients remove trust in the compromised intermediates.
